speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a significant medical history and are presenting with gait and limb ataxia; to begin my assessment, have you noticed any issues with your vision, such as double vision or a loss of vision in one eye?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That unsteadiness on the right side is concerning for a focal neurological issue; to determine if this is central or peripheral, have you noticed any weakness or numbness in your limbs, and do you have a history of stroke or diabetes?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, combined with your new onset of gait and limb ataxia, this presentation is highly suggestive of PML. I need to confirm the neurological deficits before ordering imaging. Have you noticed any new sensory changes, such as tingling or numbness, or any difficulty with speech?
